title: The AI Wrote My Report, So What Did I Do All Day?
script: Dedi: [uneasy] I finished the quarterly report in twenty minutes today. The assistant drafted most of it, I just edited the framing.
Wulan: [amused] That sounds like a good problem to have, more time for everything else.

Dedi: [conflicted] It should feel that way, but instead I spent the rest of the afternoon vaguely anxious, wondering what exactly I'm being paid for if the drafting itself takes no real skill anymore.

Wulan: [thoughtful] I've had that same unease. Though I wonder if we're mourning a version of the job that was already partly obsolete, all that time spent formatting rather than actually deciding anything.
Dedi: [considering] Maybe. But formatting felt like proof of effort, something tangible I could point to at the end of a long day.
Wulan: [pointed] Proof of effort isn't the same as proof of value, though. Nobody's paying us to look busy, however satisfying that used to feel.

Dedi: [candid] That's uncomfortably accurate. I think what actually unsettles me is that the parts I now spend my time on, judgment calls, prioritizing, pushing back on assumptions, are much harder to point to at a glance.
Wulan: [agreeing] They're invisible labor, essentially. Nobody applauds you for deciding not to pursue a flawed strategy; they just never see the disaster that didn't happen.
Dedi: [worried] Which makes me wonder how replaceable that invisible labor actually is, longer term, once the tools get better at anticipating those judgment calls too.

Wulan: [measured] Possibly, eventually. But someone still has to own the consequences of a wrong call, and I doubt organizations will ever let an algorithm absorb that kind of accountability entirely.
Dedi: [reflective] Accountability as the last human job. That's a strange thing to find reassuring, and yet somehow it is.
Wulan: [wry] Reassuring, or at least a decent argument for demanding a raise now that we're apparently the ones holding the risk.

quiz.question: How long did it take Dedi to finish the quarterly report, and why?
options: Three hours, using his usual method
Twenty minutes, because the assistant drafted most of it
All day, due to technical problems
One week, working with a team
quiz.explanation: Dedi finished the report in twenty minutes because the AI assistant drafted most of it.

options: Vaguely anxious, wondering what he is being paid for

quiz.question: What does Wulan suggest they might be mourning?
options: A version of the job that was already partly obsolete, focused on formatting rather than deciding
quiz.explanation: Wulan wonders if they're mourning a version of the job already partly obsolete, centered on formatting rather than decisions.

quiz.question: What does Wulan say about proof of effort versus proof of value?
options: Proof of effort isn't the same as proof of value; nobody pays them to look busy
Effort no longer matters at all
quiz.explanation: Wulan points out proof of effort isn't proof of value, and nobody is paid simply to look busy.

quiz.question: What do Dedi and Wulan conclude might remain a distinctly human role?
options: Owning the consequences and accountability of a wrong judgment call
quiz.explanation: They conclude accountability for consequences may remain the last distinctly human job, as organizations won't let an algorithm absorb it.
